evidence: Official license page: Godot is released under the permissive MIT license; derivative games may use any license but must include the MIT license text.
Official scripting tutorials covering GDScript, C#, and C++ via GDExtension; the engine's primary automation APIs.
zlib-licensed 3D engine shipped as a Blender add-on; Haxe scripting, logic nodes, and a fully scriptable deferred/forward renderer.
Manual states UPBGE is GNU GPL; game .blend assets remain the author's property, but standalone bundles embedding the Blender Player must be GPL-compatible.
Fork of Blender (GPLv3) with the integrated game engine restored; combines full 3D scene authoring, logic bricks, and Python game scripting in one suite.
Full C++/C# source is public but governed by the proprietary Flax EULA; source-available, not OSI open source; tool redistribution restricted to their Store or forks.
Dual Apache-2.0/MIT licensed AAA engine with the Atom physically based renderer, aimed at cinema-quality 3D worlds and simulations with no fees or commercial obligations.
Scene composition engine (layers, references, variants) for non-destructive interchange of complex 3D scenes; now under the Tomorrow Open Source Technology License 1.0, an Apache-2.0 derivative.
Official documentation hub for USD, the open format for scalable 3D interchange, with C++ and Python API references adopted across DCC pipelines.
BSD-3-licensed node-based application for lookdev, lighting and scene automation; multi-threaded deferred evaluation engine used in VFX production.
Official tutorial demonstrates building and manipulating node graphs programmatically in the built-in Python Editor, including OSL shader scripting.
AGPL-3.0 web application for production tracking in animation and VFX studios; assets, shots, tasks and deliveries managed collaboratively.
AYON core addon remains Apache-2.0 and provides pipeline base classes, publishing plugins and DCC integrations (successor to OpenPype).
AYON server moved from Apache-2.0 to the Functional Source License from v1.7.0 onward, converting to Apache-2.0 two years after each release; core and integrations stay Apache.
GPLv3 open source system for processing and editing large 3D triangle meshes; standard tool for cleaning scanned/reconstructed geometry.
GPLv3 Python bindings (pybind11) exposing MeshLab's filter library for scripted batch mesh processing.
MIT-licensed C++/Python library for 3D data processing (point clouds, meshes, registration, reconstruction) with GPU-accelerated pipelines.
MIT-licensed pure-Python library to load, query, transform and export triangular meshes across dozens of formats; widely used as a scripting layer in geometry pipelines.
MIT-licensed Python renderer implementing the glTF 2.0 physically based shading model, with offscreen OSMesa/EGL rendering for headless realistic image generation.
Open-source multi-platform geometry processing/rendering framework; plugin architecture with scripting access to all functions, relicensed to BSD-3-Clause.
Code-first parametric solid CAD (GPLv2+ with CGAL linking exception); models defined entirely by script for fully programmatic geometry generation.
LGPL-2+ parametric 3D CAD modeler with a comprehensive Python API; macros, workbenches and headless scripting drive procedural modeling.
Apache-2.0 Python library for parametric B-rep CAD built on OpenCascade; models expressed as fluent scripts, exportable to STEP/3MF/STL.
Apache-2.0 Python CAD programming library derived from CadQuery and refactored over Open Cascade; builder and algebra APIs for scripted parametric design.
GPL-3.0-or-later constraint-based parametric 2D/3D CAD with STEP import/export and simple mechanical simulation.
Source code is AGPL but bundled assets and all program output (FBX/OBJ exports, renders) are released under CC0; generated characters carry no license restrictions.
Free open-source parametric human generator running as a Blender addon; stable v2.0.8 distributed via Blender's official extension platform.
Archived community fork of ManuelBastioniLAB for Blender 4.0+; caveat: morph database is AGPL so generated models inherit AGPL, blocking closed-source use.
MIT-licensed standard Unity implementation of the glTF-based VRM 1.0 avatar format, including the MToon toon-shading system for anime-style characters.
Apache-2.0 modular PyTorch framework for NeRF and Gaussian Splatting training, with plug-in methods, viewer, and export to splats/meshes.
Apache-2.0 CUDA-accelerated differentiable rasterization library for 3D Gaussians with Python bindings; fully commercial-friendly splatting backend.
Under NVIDIA Source Code License-NC: use restricted to non-commercial research/evaluation; commercial deployment requires a separate NVIDIA license.
Original 3DGS code carries an Inria/MPII research-only license; commercial exploitation requires prior explicit consent; drives adoption of Apache alternatives like gsplat.
Commercial closed-source end-to-end radiance-field tool (tracking, training, editing, rendering splats); contrast point, open equivalents are nerfstudio/gsplat.
Kerbl et al.: 3D Gaussian scene representation achieves state-of-the-art quality with real-time (>=30 fps) novel-view synthesis at 1080p.
Mildenhall et al.: foundational paper representing scenes as neural radiance fields for photorealistic novel-view synthesis; basis of the NeRF tool ecosystem.
